newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds down, some late short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds down, some late short-covering.

text.p: Argentine bonds fell Thursday but short-covering late in the day recovered some of the losses as players felt the market had priced in a negative number in Friday's U.S. producer prices report.
"I think the market was expecting a bad number, that is why there was some short-covering late," said a trader at a local bank.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 3/8 at 89-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.12 to 128.00.
Another trader said activity was thin again, as most investors remain on the sidelines until the U.S. rate outlook becomes clearer.
The first trader said it was difficult to predict how the market will perform in coming days because "everything depends on what happens in the world."
And even if the U.S. PPI report does not have a major impact, other U.S. indicators may well convince investors that there will be more U.S rate hikes.
In the money markets, call money rates were flat at 5.83 percent.
